reviewer: Claude Code (AI assistant). Not an independent human review.
method: A sweep of every page of the year for passages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains; each passage read, looked up in the year's lists and counted by its own opening words against every page in both transcriptions, by the thin-year rule (Y-THIN as amended on 23 November 2026: items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; single paragraphs from runs of news counted by their own words, C-09); the items printed by every surviving paper admitted at the owner's word of 25 November 2026; scan checks of each admitted passage
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: New York, 13 February 1798: 'IMPORTANT and SATISFACTORY. By a gentleman of respectability, and of this City, arrived yesterday, in 18 days from New Orleans'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a New York paragraph of 13 February 1798, headed 'IMPORTANT and SATISFACTORY': 'By a gentleman of respectability, and of this City, arrived yesterday, in 18 days from New Orleans, we have the pleasing information, that the Spanish Posts at the Natchez, and other places within our territory, on the river Mississippi, had been at length given up to the American Commissioner, and the troops under his direction ...'. A New York report of a traveller's news, as the papers reprinted it; the New Hampshire Gazette prints it without the heading.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

new_groups.label: New Orleans, 15 January 1798: the Moniteur de la Louisiane: 'The Governor of this province having received by the last Courier the orders of his Majesty to evacuate the forts of Walnut Hills and Natchez'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a translated extract from the Moniteur de la Louisiane, printed at New Orleans, dated 15 January 1798: 'The Governor of this province having received by the last Courier the orders of his Majesty to evacuate the forts of Walnut Hills and Natchez, immediately took proper measures for their execution, having sent off the necessary advices for Natchez.' A New Orleans paper's notice, as the American papers reprinted it; the Mirror prints it under its own heading, 'GOOD NEWS! New-Orleans, [Spanish Territories] Jan. 15.' (C-02).
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1798. The sweep check of 24 and 25 November 2026 (X-THIN-SWEEP; outputs/story_discovery_1779/sweep_check_25nov.md) read every passage of the 1798 pages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains, looked each up in the year's lists and counted it by its own opening words against every page of the year in both transcriptions. It found two items printed by every paper that survives for their weeks, which round one's lists did not name; asked, the owner chose on 25 November 2026 to admit them as the rule reads. Every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/round2.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md; verdicts in scan_verdicts/round2*.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one (Y-THIN as amended, B1): an item printed by every newspaper that survives for its weeks is admitted. Both items are printed by all 4 papers of their weeks; they are one affair (the Spanish posts on the Mississippi), and each is admitted by its own count, as the rule's first part reads.
